prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” agency for everyone — it depends on your goals, industry, budget, timeline, and whether you want performance marketing, SEO, creative/branding, product UX, programmatic/media buying, or full-service.

Quick questions to narrow it down
- What are your primary goals? (lead gen, e‑commerce revenue, brand awareness, product launches, retention)
- What’s your monthly/annual marketing budget?
- Do you need strategy + execution, or just execution?
- Any vertical focus (SaaS, fintech, healthcare, e‑commerce, consumer)?
- Do you prefer a local SF agency or are remote/global partners fine?

How to pick the right agency (step-by-step)
1. Define measurable goals and budget.  
2. Search reputable review sites (Clutch, G2, Ad Age, The Drum) and LinkedIn for case studies in your vertical.  
3. Shortlist 3–5 agencies by specialty (performance, SEO, creative, analytics).  
4. Run a short RFP / discovery call (30–60 minutes) and ask for relevant case studies, KPIs, team bios, and a proposed 90‑day plan.  
5. Pilot with a small paid test project (1–3 months) before committing long term.

Questions to ask during vetting (important ones)
- Which clients similar to us have you helped and what results did you produce?  
- Who on your team will work with us and what’s their experience?  
- What KPIs will you optimize and how will you report progress?  
- What does success look like at 30 / 90 / 180 days?  
- What’s your pricing model and minimum contract length?  
- How do you handle creative assets and approvals?  
- Can you share references I can call?

Agencies to research in/near San Francisco (examples by specialty)
- AKQA — digital product/experience, creative & UX.  
- Goodby Silverstein & Partners — creative and brand campaigns (SF-based).  
- MightyHive — programmatic media, analytics and Google Cloud/advertising integrations (San Francisco presence).  
- Metric Theory — paid media and performance marketing (Bay Area offices).  
- Wpromote — performance marketing and paid media (national, SF office).  
- Smaller boutique options — many excellent local boutiques focus on startups, product marketing, or B2B SaaS; use Clutch/G2 and LinkedIn to find ones that match your vertical.

If you want, tell me your goals, budget, and industry and I’ll:
- recommend 3–5 agencies in San Francisco specifically matched to your needs, and  
- draft a short RFP and 30/90-day pilot scope you can send them.
